summary:
The story begins a year before the accident at issue. On September 3, 2022, the patient injured the neck during a heavy squat set at the gym, and by September 10 had begun intake at Back & Spine Restoration Center, though the record contains some discrepancy as to the exact injury date. Dr. Alistair Finch evaluated the patient on September 12, 2022, diagnosing acute cervical strain with possible underlying disc herniation or bulge, and noting prior treatment for cervicalgia that same year. A three-view cervical X-ray on September 15, 2022 confirmed mild degenerative disc disease at C6-C7 with a 4mm posterior disc bulge — a finding later flagged by both Dr. Elizabeth Foster and Dr. Myrtle Turner as a pre-existing condition documented before the motor vehicle accident that follows.

That accident occurred on or before September 4, 2023, producing fractures of the left humerus and radius. Dr. Elizabeth Foster performed emergency open reduction and internal fixation that day under nerve block anesthesia at Littel Inc Emergency Hospital; a head CT followed on September 5, and fluoroscopic imaging confirmed hardware placement on September 7 under Dr. Myrtle Turner. Acetaminophen 975mg managed pain during the admission.

Discharged with diagnoses of post-surgical left humerus/radius ORIF, cervicalgia, and a left knee contusion, the patient began physical therapy at Lang-Weimann Medical Center on September 15, 2023 under Dr. Marcus Chen. Early sessions repeatedly provoked cervical symptoms during wrist stretching and traction work. Turner removed surgical staples on September 21 and started Oxycodone-Acetaminophen 5-325mg, later adding Cyclobenzaprine 10mg on October 19 for spasm and Ibuprofen 800mg on November 16 as inflammation and neck pain worsened. X-ray on October 19 showed early callus formation, but grip strength remained weak and stiffness significant. The patient then missed three consecutive PT sessions between November 14 and November 21, and elbow stiffness rebounded sharply on return November 24, requiring intensified passive stretching. Thirty sessions concluded December 11 with persistent cervical stiffness and arm pain; Turner ordered MRI of the left upper extremity and C-spine on December 14, by which point X-rays showed well-healed fractures with stable hardware despite decreased radial sensation.

Care transferred to Amanda Gregory at Emory Sports Medicine Complex on January 8, 2024, for continued cervicalgia and muscle wasting. Over 30 sessions through March 22, cervical symptoms were repeatedly provoked despite progressive strengthening work. Turner's February 8 follow-up confirmed complete bony fusion but limited shoulder and forearm range of motion. By discharge on March 25, 2024, the patient had achieved substantial gains but retained a persistent 15-degree extension deficit in the left elbow and chronic pain, an outcome complicated throughout by a disc bulge with roots predating the collision.
